main_text.p: cludit: Ergo laude dignus est. Hic est secundus Syl-logismus practicus, specialis ille. Hunc Syllogismum specialem in mente Hectoris secuta est lætitia, quæ ipsius animum in gravissimis periculis non parum le-niebat, imò liberabat adeò, ut mori pro patriâ jam non pertimuerit. Nam cùm à vate Polydamante ad-moneretur, ne bellum contra Græcos iniret, respon-dit:
Εἷς οἰωνὸς ἄριστος[?], ἀμύνεσθαι[?] περὶ πάτρης.

p.i: Adeò præstans ille heros conscientiâ facti fretus, se ad-versus ærumnas in periculis pro defendendâ patriâ susceptis erexit. Nam cùm vates volatum avium si-gnificare triστem eventum nunciaret, Hector animo-sè respondit: sive dextrorsum aves ortum versus, sive sinistrorsum ad occasum volent,

main_text.p: Ἡμεῖς δὴ μεγάλοιο Διὸς πειθώμεθα βουλῇ. Consilium Jovis appellans impetum animi heroicum, quo ad rem praeclarè & honestè gerendam impelleba-tur. Non enim putabat ullum tempus esse, quo ea, quae honesta sunt, non sint facienda, præsertim cùm salus patriæ agitur. Nam juxta Euripidis sententiam, τὸ καλὸν φίλον ἀεί.

Rursus συλλήψις OEdipo hanc propositionem suppeditavit: Turpissima facta gravissimis pœnis sunt Syllogis-mus practi-cus aecu-sans.digna. Lex naturæ formavit hanc minorem: Incestus cum matre concubitus & parricidiū sunt turpissima facta. τὸ [?] conclusit: Ergo incestus cum matre concubitus & parricidium dignissima sunt gravissimis pœnis. Hic est Syllogismus practicus primus, adhuc generalis: quem statim sequitur specialis, in quo συλ-λήψεως resumit conclusionem Syllogismi generalis, nicē-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "ἄριστος" and "ἀμύνεσθαι" in the first Greek line are partly obscured by print damage. The Greek in the last line is copied as seen, accents included. Italic and roman type were judged from the scan. The word "tristem" in the Latin line above has a letter that is not fully clear; it is read as "tristem", i.e. triste, with the mark [?] applied if the reading is doubtful. The Greek word after "Rursus" is read as συλλήψις with doubt. The Greek word after "minorem" and the Greek word in the last line are not fully legible, so they are marked [?]. The abbreviation on "parricidiū" is doubtful. The last word "nicē-" is read with doubt at the line end.
